gap: No result ChatGPT got (of the six I could open) states that RTINGS bench-tested the MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro and confirmed it uses its full 8,000 Hz polling rate with no latency bottleneck, or that no named lab has published a latency figure for the Gamakay NS68, Aula WIN60 HE or Epomaker HE68 Lite.
standout_why: Compared against hlplanet.com (cited), mechanicalkeyboard.net's HE68 Lite review (cited), mechanicalkeyboard.net's budget guide, chronicreload.com and gamepadsquire.com's NS68 review. HLPlanet already carries part of this angle: its own OSLTT figure of 0.3 ms for the MCHOSE Ace 68 and 'very low latency' (no number) for the MCHOSE Ace 60. The other four give only maker specs or 0.125 ms arithmetic from 8,000 Hz. RTINGS's ms figures for the Ace 60 Pro are locked behind membership, so this angle adds a named lab's wording and no new number. PC Gamer's two pages (one cited) returned only navigation, and I did not open deal.ai, setupinsider, thepcjournal, pricepect, computerstationnation, checkgamingzone or droid4x, so the gap is not checked against those.
decides: It supports ChatGPT's MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro pick for wired FPS: it is the only candidate a named lab (RTINGS) has bench-tested, and RTINGS calls it wired-only. This holds only if its price today is under $50, which I did not read. For the Gamakay NS68 (the one board under $50 we can link, $36.79 wired / $39.99 tri-mode in the partner table), there is no named latency measurement, so the page must not claim measured latency for it. Any segment win for the NS68 has to rest on price and wireless, not measurements; HLPlanet's summary names it the cheapest wireless option. Without a readable ms figure this angle should not lead the page.
